blocks.text: One of the most important applications of retrosynthesis is in pharmaceutical product synthesis. There are hundreds of valuable medicinal compounds, which look very complex in their structure, but if they are disconnected properly and efficiently, we can approach to very simple and commonly available starting materials. This is the beauty of organic synthesis, that it makes the highly complex and terrifying structure, look so simple and achievable after a series of efficient retrosynthetic steps. In the following we will discuss synthesis of some common pharmaceutical products.
Example 25.3.1 Paracetamol (TM)
Direct Synthesis of Paracetamol

blocks.alt: Phenol (HO on a benzene ring) followed by four short arrows labelled 'A series of steps' leading to paracetamol, HO on a benzene ring with N(H)-C(=O)-CH3 at the opposite position.
blocks.caption: Direct synthesis of paracetamol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 139).

blocks.text: It can be seen that direct synthesis of paracetamol requires a series of steps. This series of steps can be decoded by its retrosynthesis as follows,
Retrosynthesis of Paracetamol
Step I Disconnection
The first step is the disconnection of paracetamol from C—N bond in amide group to get synthons.
Step II Synthetic Equivalents (SE)
These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., 4-aminophenol and acyl chloride molecule.
The bond is broken at the position indicated because the synthetic equivalents of the resulting synthons are well known to react through a nucleophilic addition-elimination reaction.
Step III Functional group interconversion
FGI has been done because it is easy to prepare p-nitrophenol and it can then be reduced to p-aminophenol.
Step IV Disconnection
Then disconnection of 4-aminophenol was done from C—N bond, which created synthons of 4-hyrodxy aryl anion (C₆H₅⁻) and nitronium (NO₂⁺) cation.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Step IV disconnects 4-nitrophenol (the molecule drawn in the scheme), not 4-aminophenol. The 4-hydroxy aryl anion is HO–C₆H₄⁻, not C₆H₅⁻ as printed.
Step V Synthetic Equivalents (SE)
These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., benzene and nitric acid molecule.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The synthetic equivalents in Step V are phenol (for the 4-hydroxy aryl anion) and nitric acid, as the scheme shows; the text prints “benzene”.

blocks.alt: Five steps. I: paracetamol with a wavy slash on the amide C-N bond, Disconnection, gives HO-C6H4-N(-)H, synthon (A), plus +C(=O)CH3, synthon (B). II: synthon (A) equals 4-aminophenol (SE); synthon (B) equals acyl chloride (SE). III: 4-aminophenol, FGI open arrow, 4-nitrophenol. IV: 4-nitrophenol slashed at the C-NO2 bond gives HO-C6H4 with a negative charge, synthon (A), plus NO2+, synthon (B). V: these equal phenol (SE) and nitric acid HO-NO2 (SE).
blocks.caption: Retrosynthesis of paracetamol, Steps I-V (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 139-140).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Step III of the printed scheme uses a forward reaction arrow from 4-aminophenol to 4-nitrophenol; a functional group interconversion in retrosynthesis takes the open retrosynthetic arrow, as drawn above.
Synthesis of Paracetamol
Paracetamol will then be synthesized according to the following scheme.

blocks.alt: Phenol, labelled phenol (SM), with HNO3 over and H2SO4 under the arrow gives 4-nitrophenol; Sn + HCl gives 4-aminophenol; a downward arrow labelled CH3COCl gives paracetamol, labelled Paracetamol (TM).
blocks.caption: Synthesis of paracetamol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).

blocks.text: Example 25.3.2 Aspirin (Acetylsalicylic Acid) TM
Direct Synthesis of Aspirin

blocks.alt: Phenol followed by four short arrows labelled 'A series of steps' leading to aspirin: a benzene ring with COOH and, on the neighbouring carbon, O-C(=O)-CH3.
blocks.caption: Direct synthesis of aspirin (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).

blocks.text: Just like Paracetamol the direct synthesis of Aspirin also requires a series of steps. By retrosynthesis we can truly find how many and which steps are actually needed to prepare Aspirin from phenol (simple starting material).
Retrosynthesis of Aspirin
Retrosynthetic Tree
Step I Disconnection-I
The first step is the disconnection of Aspirin from C—O bond in ester linkage to get synthons.
Step II Synthetic Equivalents (SE)
These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., salicylic acid and acetic anhydride molecule.
Step III Disconnection-II
Next disconnection is the C—C bond of carboxylic group.
Step IV Synthetic Equivalents (SE)
These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., phenol and carbon dioxide molecule.

blocks.alt: Four steps. I: aspirin (TM) with a wavy slash on the ester O-C bond, Disconnection, gives the 2-carboxyphenoxide ion, synthon (A), plus +C(=O)CH3, synthon (B). II: synthon (A) equals salicylic acid (SE); synthon (B) equals acetic anhydride (SE). III: salicylic acid slashed at the ring-COOH bond gives a ring carbanion next to OH, (A) synthon, plus +C(=O)OH, (B) synthon. IV: these equal phenol (SE) and carbon dioxide O=C=O (SE).
blocks.caption: Retrosynthesis of aspirin, Steps I-IV (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 141).

blocks.text: Synthesis of Aspirin
Aspirin will then be synthesized according to the following scheme.

blocks.alt: Phenol (SM) with (i) CO2, High T & P over and (ii) H2SO4 under the arrow gives salicylic acid; acetic anhydride drawn over and H3PO4, Heat under the next arrow gives Aspirin (TM).
blocks.caption: Synthesis of aspirin (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 141).

blocks.title: Quick Check 25.3
blocks.text:
Aspirin and Paracetamol, both are synthesized starting from phenol.
I) What is the overall functional group difference in them?
ii) In synthesis of which FGI (Functional Group Interconversion) is involved?
iii) Which synthon is common in preparation of them? Write down its structure and also mention its most common synthetic equivalent.
